rules: Use the same profile for every capacity-verifier platform. It controls only the independent Python/OpenUSD verifier's pool, not native Rust operations or global user settings.
Set the environment before importing pxr. Do not initialize any USD or NumPy module before the original complete wall clock.
Inside the existing initialize task, import pxr.Work and require GetConcurrencyLimit()==1 and HasConcurrency()==false. Record effective and physical limits. A mismatched profile is failure.

The same complete validated native projection, durable export, actual fresh native query, all exact/source1e-6 comparisons, module initialization, every future result and worker join remain inside their original clocks.
All six original samples and250/500ms core and2000/4000ms total limits remain. No cooldown, preclock warmup, averaging, discarded sample, cached result or hardware exemption.
NumPy's existing ufunc comparisons and arithmetic stay unchanged. No new BLAS operation, reassociation or numeric tolerance is introduced.
Record available disk space with the existing host/environment evidence. CPU/RSS/thread diagnostics never decide success or excuse a failed sample.
Oversubscription or host contention is a hypothesis, not an established cause. Only actual new complete samples can establish a pass. All prior failures remain.
source_rule: The pinned26.05 Work setting0 permits maximum physical concurrency. Setting1 requests single-threaded mode and takes precedence over runtime API limits. The pinned wheel has the Work Python module and its wrapper exposes GetConcurrencyLimit and HasConcurrency. Static inspection is not runtime proof; CI must assert the effective limit.
